lattice-bead / 3.frag · overnight run

Mon Lattice Presets

Japanese mon as the repeating cell of a music-reactive lattice. The test is recognition: a stranger, at a distance, in a dark room, should be able to name their own bead. Tap anything to play it — tiles are frozen frames (time=8) so the comparison is honest, links are live and audio-reactive.

The eleven beads

An earlier version of this page claimed all eleven were nameable. That was wrong — an art critic judging the grid cold scored it 4 clear, 2 arguable, 5 failed. Since then the interior structure (eroded gaps and trend rings) has made tomoe, ogi and katabami read, and separated suhama from katabami. One pair still fails: kikyo and ume, and that is a source‑art problem rather than a shader one — see below. These tiles are re‑rendered on detail.frag at the corrected palette.

Why it was failing, and the fix

The cause was figure/ground. 3.frag deliberately let the lattice texture survive inside the motif — its own comment calls that a feature. But interior and exterior then carry the same contrast, so the eye has no silhouette to lock onto and the shape never resolves. The measurements agreed: 76.1% common effect with only 7.9pt of between‑motif spread.

4.frag adds one hand lever, legible, which collapses the interior toward the bead’s own ink, deepens the ground recede, and widens the contour into a drawn line. Every term is mask‑bound and spatially structured — no global multiplier, so none of it can strobe — and it is a hand knob, so no geometry moves with the music.

knob_169 0.60 navZoom 0.14 legible 1 knob_168 1.0
Cell size is a prerequisite — and it is a window, not a maximum. Past 0.75 the camera sits inside a single bead and the silhouette is gone entirely.

Two parameters are not optional

?wavelet=true — without it all seven wavelet springs read exactly 0.000, so bassLive, midsLive and trebLive are dead and most of the shader is deaf. The synthetic bench pins these, so it is structurally blind to this and will never catch it.

?onset_refractory_ms=380 — at the default the onset detector free-runs at about 213 BPM, chasing hats instead of the kick.

What the sweep settled

Two of these are negative results. They are the more useful ones — they close off directions that look promising and are not.

Actionable

The shipped default is the weakest column

paletteShift=1.7 is the current default, and across all four themes it produces the washed pink‑lilac you flagged as “fuzzy terrible fuchsia”. The strong looks sit at 0.45 (deep cyan), 1.05 (ember) and 1.35 (jade).

Theme 3 washes out across every hue — its lightness scale of 1.20 blows the pastel.

Partly solved

Figure/ground fixed most of it — kikyo and ume are source art

Flattening the interior and carving eroded gaps made tomoe, ogi and katabami read, and lifted suhama vs katabami to the separation of a pair that passes.

kikyo vs ume cannot be fixed in the shader. Erosion rings follow the outline, so they cannot separate shapes whose outlines already match — and measured on the baked artwork itself, the two are 4–7× more alike than any other pair (radial profile distance 0.019, against 0.079 and 0.141). kikyo’s petals measure no sharper than ume’s. The generator documents widening its shoulders and opening the tip to ~67°, and says outright that the difference from ume is now only the tip. That softening erased it.

Correction

The palette these were first shown in crushed 13% of pixels

Every earlier tile on this page was rendered with theme=0 & paletteShift=1.35 — the jet‑colormap look the critic called “the visual signature of nobody having made a decision”. Measured later, it also crushes 13% of pixels to a dead channel, the worst gamut behaviour of any variant.

The bare default measures 0% crush at comparable contrast, and on live audio has less than half the flash. Everything here is re‑rendered on it, and every preset in the shader moved off the old one.

Method

Five times, a null result was the instrument

A whole‑frame metric could not see an effect touching 1/11 of the beads. Luminance and contrast are blind to direction. Downsampling a 1278px canvas to 90px diluted a 1px hairline 200×. And a still frame cannot measure flash at all — which is how a palette got recommended here that turned out to be the flashiest of the set.

The rule that came out of it: name the property being judged, then check the instrument has that axis. Contrast is spatial, flash is temporal, asymmetry is directional, a hairline is high‑frequency. An instrument missing the axis still returns a confident number — about something else.

Negative result

Seed pitch is a dead lever

knob_169 swept 0.10 → 0.55 against knob_168 at 0.55/0.9/1.0 gave fifteen near‑identical tiles.

The cause, found afterwards: that sweep omitted navZoom and dropped lattice-nav, pinning the framing. navZoom is the framing lever; knob_169 only sets pitch within a framing.

No shudder

Measured on live audio — 1289 frames of the running set, not a synthetic bench.

Per‑frame jitter of each candidate drive signal. Normalised by range — raw jitter flatters whichever signal happens to have the smaller span, which is how an earlier version of this table overstated the result by 4×.

Corrected: the flare is about 1.7× smoother than the z‑score once range is accounted for — not the 6.8× first claimed here, which compared raw jitter across signals with very different spans. The real win was never smoothness anyway, it was latency: smoothing a level enough to stop the shudder costs roughly a second of lag, and an event-driven envelope costs none. Tempo lock moved from beat at 280 BPM to 125.3 BPM — the set’s actual tempo — with a 3% gap spread.
